probe.question: Can the OCI Distribution CAS act as a passive hash-native route from Git commit 573f2f0a00718109e2cd2fc1c1c9bf2f5a0404de to independently pre-existing exact content without unknown repository/index discovery, external mutation, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, incremental cost, protected authority or manual user action?

sources.observed: Blob pull and existence checks are addressed as /v2/<name>/blobs/<digest>; <name> is the repository namespace. The spec also defines digest as a cryptographic content identifier and permits registries to reject unsupported digest algorithms.

A traditional Git object SHA-1 names the SHA-1 of type, length, NUL and the object's SHA-1 content; Git SHA-256 naming is a distinct object-name mapping, not derivable as a generic alternate CAS digest from the SHA-1 name alone without object/mapping data.

probe.tested_scope: Specification-level falsification of OCI Distribution as a global passive commit-hash lookup route for the exact Git commit ID above. No registry was mutated, no target residency was assumed, and no repository namespace/provider was supplied.

comparison.success_probability_for_exact_target_wit: LOW/FAIL under the tested scope because a registry host and repository <name> remain required in addition to <digest>
comparison.integration_cost: LOW only when registry and repository namespace are already known; unresolved for unknown-residency discovery
comparison.quota_fragility: No quota consumed in this audit; registry-specific limits are irrelevant because the route already fails the namespace-free discovery gate

reasoning_summary: OCI content addressing solves integrity once a registry repository and digest are known, but the normative pull endpoint requires both a repository namespace and a digest.
The exact Git commit SHA-1 therefore does not by itself determine the OCI registry host or repository namespace, so unknown-index/repository discovery remains unresolved.

A Git SHA-1 also does not establish that an independently pre-existing OCI blob is stored under a compatible digest representation; any packaging/upload convention or external publication would violate this probe's passive pre-existing-residency requirement.
This separates content-address integrity from global provider/repository discovery: a viable transversal route must couple both under a hash-only lookup key.

Hash-native exact binding alone is insufficient; the next candidate must also provide provider/location discovery keyed solely by the Git commit hash or a deterministic key derived from it.
